record.context_brief: Classification of optimal rank-metric variants over rings of order 4
record.original_question: Classify all linear codes over rings of order 4 that meet the corresponding rank bounds for Lee, Euclidean, or Bachoc weight, namely all MLDR, MEDR, and MBDR codes.

evidence.quote: A code meeting bound (1) is a Maximum Lee Distance with respect to Rank (MLDR) Code, a code meeting bound (2) is a Maximum Euclidean Distance with respect to Rank (MEDR) Code, a code over meeting bound (3) is a Maximum Bachoc Distance with respect to Rank (MBDR) Code.
Open Question 6.6. Find and classify all MLDR, MEDR, MBDR codes over rings of order 4.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let R be a finite ring of order 4 (for instance Z/4Z or F_2[u]/(u^2) or F_4). Consider linear codes C ⊆ R^n. Three weight functions are considered on R:

(i) the Lee weight w_L,
(ii) the Euclidean weight w_E,
(iii) the Bachoc weight w_B.

For a codeword x ∈ R^n, define the corresponding distance d_•(x) as the sum of the per-coordinate weights, and for a code C set d_•(C) = min{d_•(x) : x ∈ C, x ≠ 0}. Each codeword x ∈ R^n also has a rank rk(x), defined (as in the rank-metric setting for codes over rings of order 4) via the matrix associated to x over the underlying prime field; the rank distance of a code is rk(C) = min{rk(x) : x ∈ C, x ≠ 0}.

Known bounds relate the Lee, Euclidean, and Bachoc distances of a linear code to its rank K and length n:
  (1)  d_L(C) ≤ Φ_L(n,K),
  (2)  d_E(C) ≤ Φ_E(n,K),
  (3)  d_B(C) ≤ Φ_B(n,K),
for explicit functions Φ_L, Φ_E, Φ_B (the rank-metric Singleton-type bounds for these weights).

A code attaining bound (1) is called a Maximum Lee Distance with respect to Rank (MLDR) code; attaining (2) gives a Maximum Euclidean Distance with respect to Rank (MEDR) code; attaining (3) gives a Maximum Bachoc Distance with respect to Rank (MBDR) code.

Problem: Find and classify, up to equivalence, all MLDR, MEDR, and MBDR linear codes over every ring of order 4.
artifact.status_search_result: A recent preprint (arXiv:2408.11107, updated June 2025) studies bounds on MLDR codes over Z_{p^t} and provides constructions, but does not give a complete classification of MLDR, MEDR, and MBDR codes over all rings of order 4. The classification problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Bounds on MLDR Codes Over Z_{p^t}
status_evidence.snippet: An MLDR (Maximum Lee Distance with respect to Rank) code is a code C ⊆ (Z_{p^t})^n of rank K satisfying d_L(C) = Φ(n,K,p^t). The paper provides bounds and constructions, not a full classification.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses bounds/constructions but not the full classification over rings of order 4.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Coding Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Open Question 6.6. Find and classify all MLDR, MEDR, MBDR codes over rings of order 4.
